official.description_text:
Postdoc in Information Theoretic Analysis of Machine Learning Methods
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to strengthen our research environment and to contribute to fundamental research on the theoretical foundations of machine learning and decision-making. Your primary goal in this role will be to develop your research profile through both independent work and collaboration with colleagues in the department.
The position is based in the Department of Information Science and Engineering within the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
A strong background in information theory and learning theory.
Excellent academic track record and potential as well as well-developed analytical and problem-solving skills.
Documented track record of successful research grant applications.
Ability to work independently.
Excellent skills in English, both oral and in writing
as this will be required in day-to-day work.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.
Trade union representatives
Contact information to
trade union representatives.
To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.
A
position as a postdoctoral fellow
is a time-limited qualified appointment focusing mainly on research, intended as a first career step after a dissertation.

In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in theoretical foundations of machine learning, focusing on information-theoretic analysis at KTH Stockholm. Research is independent and theoretical, emphasizing learning theory and information theory.

thematic_fit.rationale: Minimal thematic connection. Position focuses on pure machine learning theory and information theory. Researcher's domain is human-centred immersive systems, spatial cognition, and collaborative learning. While both relate broadly to 'learning,' the position is fundamentally algorithmic and abstract; the researcher's work is empirical and human-focused. No overlapping research questions or problem spaces.

methodological_fit.rationale: Weak methodological connection. Position requires theoretical analysis, information theory, and learning theory expertise. Researcher's methods are empirical: user studies, experimental design, questionnaires, task-based measurement. The analytical frameworks are incompatible. Researcher has no background in information theory, learning theory, or theoretical machine learning.

growth_value.rationale: Minimal growth value. Machine learning theory and information-theoretic analysis do not advance human-centred XR research, spatial learning methodology, or collaborative immersive systems design. Would not close capability gaps relevant to target identity.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH Stockholm is in Sweden (preferred country), providing geographic and institutional credibility. However, the Department of Information Science and Engineering operates in a pure CS/theory track disconnected from HCI, XR, or human-centred computing research. Would not build networks or profile toward human-centred immersive systems trajectory.

eligibility_flags: Researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress); position requires PhD. Not currently eligible unless degree is completed and conferred before employment decision.
Strong background in information theory and learning theory required. Researcher has neither.

Documented track record of successful research grant applications required. Researcher's publications are ongoing (1 first-author journal article, systematic mapping review in progress); grant application record unclear.
Preferred: PhD obtained within last 3 years; researcher has not completed PhD.
risks: PhD eligibility gap: researcher must complete degree before appointment.
Severe expertise gap: position requires deep theoretical foundations (information theory, learning theory) that researcher has no background in.
Research community mismatch: theoretical ML/information science group has no overlap with HCI, XR, or human-centred computing communities.

Independent research expectation: position emphasizes independent research track record and grant success. Researcher has limited publication record (1 first-author journal article) and unproven grant competitiveness.
Career narrative risk: 2-year theoretical ML postdoc would create distance from human-centred XR research and require substantial re-positioning for future HCI applications.
High failure risk in research productivity: researcher would lack foundational theory knowledge to generate novel contributions in information-theoretic ML analysis.
